extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, industry stakeholders, policymakers, and others interested in SEC rulemaking and administrative-law challenges
extracted.subtask_description: A press-release–style announcement and summary of a manufacturer's legal challenge to the SEC's rescission of parts of its 2020 proxy-advisor rule, emphasizing procedural and substantive defects alleged under the Administrative Procedure Act and the notice-and-comment requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Procedure Act obligations / arbitrary and capricious standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency actions must be supported by substantive justification and cannot be arbitrary or capricious under the Administrative Procedure Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NAM asserts: “The SEC has failed to provide any substantive justification for its dramatic about-face.” The press release describes the SEC’s final rescission as epitomizing “arbitrary and capricious” rulemaking and frames lack of substantive justification as a central legal defect to be challenged in court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required notice-and-comment rulemaking process
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies are required to follow the notice-and-comment process in issuing, suspending, or rescinding rules; bypassing that process is inappropriate or unlawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NAM voiced concern about the agency’s “efforts to bypass the required notice-and-comment process to keep this lawfully issued rule on ice indefinitely.” The press release treats compliance with notice-and-comment as a procedural baseline that the SEC allegedly disregarded when suspending enforcement and proposing rescissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawful suspension and enforcement of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspending enforcement of a lawfully issued rule must have lawful basis and cannot be used to indefinitely avoid the rule’s effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC’s June 2021 suspension of enforcement of the 2020 rule is described as something the NAM challenged in court (filed suit in October 2021), indicating the view that enforcement suspensions are subject to judicial review when they effectively nullify a lawfully issued rule without proper process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accountability for proxy advisory firms
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory reform should enhance transparency and accountability of proxy advisory firms to limit outsized influence and protect stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2020 SEC regulations are characterized as intended “to enhance transparency and accountability for proxy firms.” NAM frames these features as beneficial—calling the rule a “long-sought, major win for the industry and millions of manufacturing workers”—and seeks to preserve the rule’s critical components against rescission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing and procedural participation by interested stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties (e.g., industry groups) may move to intervene or otherwise participate in litigation challenging agency action to protect their interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NAM filed a motion to intervene in ISS v. SEC and later filed suits (e.g., NAM v. SEC) challenging suspension and rescission, illustrating the procedural avenue of intervention and litigation as a mechanism for stakeholders to defend regulatory protections.
